move: lines collide from opposite sides, squash on landing, snap out
how: A sunset photo drifts under a dark gradient (scale 1.08 to 1.14, xPercent -1.5 to 1.5, linear across the 2s) behind three stacked uppercase lines in clipped rows. Line one slides in from xPercent -140 (expo.out, 0.55s) at 2.5%, line two from xPercent 140 at 9%, line three rises from yPercent 120 at 16%. At 31% the middle line takes the collision shock: scaleX 1.12 / scaleY 0.86 relaxing to 1 with elastic.out(1,0.45). From 77% the lines snap out in reverse order with expo.in over 0.3s each, line three up, line two left, line one right, so the loop ends on the moving photo.
adapt: Change the three words, the accent colour on the middle line and the background photo. Keep the 0.55s expo.out entries at 0.13s spacing and the elastic squash; shorten only the hold if the copy is longer.
port: mount(el, shot) creates .bg from shot.image plus the three .row/.line pairs; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same tweens at 0.025D, 0.09D, 0.16D, 0.31D and the exit from 0.77D. Scope '.line.a' etc. to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built after first paint
